text.text: Region pile-up
The pile-up's own tables (regions and calls) come from seanome/2024-kmerseek-analysis at commit 39d81ec9 (results/leaderboard/pileup).

Where each tool's calls fall around a known domain. A call is a stretch of a human protein that a tool matched to a zebrafish protein carrying a Pfam domain. The call names that domain and spans the whole matched stretch, which can be much wider than the domain itself. Every row below is one region: one of the 2,435 Pfam domains on the 998 human query proteins. Every panel is one tool and setting searching the zebrafish proteome (zebrafish and human last shared an ancestor about 430 million years ago), and every panel has the same rows.
Data from 15 Oct 2026, commit 4a4b1171 (source)

A residue counts as covered when a call naming that region's own Pfam family spans it, at any score the tool reported (E-value cutoff 10). Covered does not mean correctly placed: a call that runs far past the domain still covers it. Each row shows 100 residues before the region, then the region itself stretched or squeezed into 100 equal steps, then 100 residues after it, as deepTools does for genes. Each step shows the residue at its centre; the median region is 89 aa, so one step is about 0.9 aa.

The order is set by one panel and used in all of them, so the rows line up across panels. In the other panels the same order can look like scattered stripes. Identity is the best pairwise identity between the human domain and any zebrafish domain of its family. Regions with no such domain, or no matching AlphaFold model, sort last.
Loading 23 panels…

Figure 3. Calls piled up around 2,435 Pfam regions, one panel per tool and setting. At the top of each panel is the share of regions covered at each position (the column average). A tool that covers the region and nothing around it draws a high step between the start and end lines. Below it, every region as a row, squeezed to fit; darker means more of the rows in that band are covered. Click a panel to draw it full size below, one pixel row per region.

The numbers under each panel: missed is the share of regions with no covered residue inside them (lower is better). Inside is the mean coverage inside the region (higher is better). Flanks is the mean coverage in the 100 residues either side. For placing domain boundaries lower is better, though a second copy of the same domain nearby counts as covered too. 0.8→0.2 is how many residues the curve takes to fall from 0.8 to 0.2 at each end of the region: fewer residues means a sharper edge. "Not reached" means the curve never gets to 0.8 inside the region; "does not fall that far" means it stays above 0.2 for all 100 residues outside.

Counts: 2,429 of the 2,435 regions have at least one residue inside their protein's sequence; the readouts use those. With one region per Pfam family (1,089 families), the region kept is the first by protein accession, then start. 9 Pfam regions run partly or wholly past the end of the protein sequence this run searched, so their Pfam coordinates belong to a different version of the sequence.

Figure 3, chosen panel: . Hover a row to see its protein, domain, coordinates, calls and residues.
Where calls start

Figure 4. For each region with a call, take the call that overlaps it most (ties go to the higher score, then the earlier start). Subtract the region's first residue from the call's first residue. 0 means the call starts on the domain's first residue; negative values start early. One line per tool, as a share of that tool's regions with a call (n in the key), in 5-residue steps; the end bins hold everything beyond 100 residues. For kmerseek the line is its setting with the highest Fmax (the best balance of precision and recall, see Methods) against zebrafish, gbmr4_k21_lcFalse. Among the aligners, between 45% (phmmer) and 60% (ProstT5 + Foldseek) of calls start more than 100 residues early. That is because a call spans the whole matched stretch. hmmscan's calls start on the domain because Pfam's domains are defined by the models hmmscan runs. Where calls end is not drawn.
